name: Caro-Kann Defense
summary: The ultra-solid positional fortress favored by World Champions Capablanca, Botvinnik, Karpov, and Anand. Black supports d5 with c6, avoiding the 'bad bishop' problem of the French Defense.
keyConcepts: Developing light bishop outside pawn chain (Bf5/Bg4)

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Classical: Capablanca Variation
subVariations.description: The quintessential Caro-Kann. Black brings the bishop out to f5 before playing ...e6, achieving a rock-solid pawn structure and great endgame chances.
subVariations.whitePlan: Castle queenside, utilize kingside space with h4-h5, target e6.
subVariations.blackPlan: Coordinate pieces smoothly, castle kingside, counterattack on queenside with ...c5.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Advance: Shirov Attack (3.e5 Bf5 4.Nc3)
subVariations.description: Alexei Shirov's ultra-aggressive setup with g4 and h4, attempting to trap or harass Black's light-squared bishop.
subVariations.whitePlan: Overrun Black's kingside with g4/h4/Nf4, win the bishop pair.
subVariations.blackPlan: Counter in the center with ...c5 and ...Nc6, exploit White's weakened king safety.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Advance: Short System (4.Nf3 e6 5.Be2)
subVariations.description: Nigel Short's sophisticated positional treatment, maintaining smooth piece coordination and queenside pressure.
subVariations.whitePlan: Develop solidly with Be2/O-O, sacrifice b2 pawn for massive initiative with Qe1/Nb5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Pressure d4 with ...c5, grab b2 with ...Qb6, pin with ...Bb4.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Advance: Tal Variation (3.e5 Bf5 4.h4)
subVariations.description: Mikhail Tal's direct 4.h4 thrust, clamping Black's bishop and threatening g4/f4.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control h5 square, sacrifice d4 pawn for active diagonals, mate the king.
subVariations.blackPlan: Halt h4 with 4...h5, attack b2 with ...Qb6, undermine center with ...c5.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack: Main Line (4.c4)
subVariations.description: Vasily Panov and Mikhail Botvinnik's dynamic weapon, blowing open the c- and d-files with 4.c4.
subVariations.whitePlan: Use active minor pieces on d3/c2 and open e-file to attack Black's king.
subVariations.blackPlan: Blockade the d5 square, fianchetto bishop on b7, exploit White's d4 IQP.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Panov: 5...Nc6 6.Nf3 Bg4 System
subVariations.description: Hyper-tactical line where Black pins with ...Bg4 and counterstrikes with ...Nxd4, dragging White's king into play.
subVariations.whitePlan: Exploit Black's king centralization on e7, maintain queenside pawn majority.
subVariations.blackPlan: Centralize knight on d4, trade queens with ...Qd7, exploit White's shattered pawns.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Steinitz (Modern) 4...Nd7
subVariations.description: Anatoly Karpov's favorite setup. Black avoids bishop exchanges with 4...Nd7, preparing ...Ngf6 without doubled pawns.
subVariations.whitePlan: Sacrifice on e6 or f7 with Ng5, attack the uncastled black king with Qg4.
subVariations.blackPlan: Defend king with ...Kf8, develop smoothly with ...Nf6 and ...b6/Bb7, counterattack.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Fantasy / Tartakower Variation (3.f3)
subVariations.description: White plays 3.f3 to maintain a full central pawn duo, leading to explosive piece sacrifices on f7.
subVariations.whitePlan: Sacrifice on f7 to expose Black's king, regain piece with e5 fork.
subVariations.blackPlan: Counterstrike in the center with ...e5, maintain active piece defense, consolidate.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Two Knights: 3...Bg4 Line
subVariations.description: Black trades the light-squared bishop for White's f3-knight to establish an impenetrable pawn fortress.
subVariations.whitePlan: Utilize bishop pair and broad center to pressure kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Coordinate knights on f6/d7, maintain solid e6/c6 base, prepare ...c5 break.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Two Knights: 3...dxe4 Line
subVariations.description: Black trades pawns on e4 and offers repeated queen trades, entering a favorable queenless middlegame.
subVariations.whitePlan: Keep queens on board with Qf4/Qe3, develop with b3 and Bb2.
subVariations.blackPlan: Force queen trade with ...Qe6, develop bishop to f5, control light squares.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Exchange Variation (3.exd5 cxd5 4.Bd3)
subVariations.description: Bobby Fischer's favorite positional line. White avoids theoretical duels and plays for a Carlsbad minority attack in reverse.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control e5 outpost with Ne5, prepare kingside expansion with f4.
subVariations.blackPlan: Execute minority attack on queenside with ...b5-b4, pressure c3 pawn.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Bronstein-Larsen: 4...Nf6 5.Nxf6+ gxf6
subVariations.description: David Bronstein and Bent Larsen's dynamic weapon. Black ruins own pawn structure with ...gxf6 to gain the open g-file.
subVariations.whitePlan: Target Black's doubled f-pawns, castle kingside, play Nh4 to win bishop pair.
subVariations.blackPlan: Attack along open g-file with ...Rg8, castle queenside, create kingside threats.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Korchnoi / Tartakower: 5...exf6
subVariations.description: Viktor Korchnoi's solid system where Black recaptures 5...exf6, achieving fast piece development and iron king safety.
subVariations.whitePlan: Develop smoothly with Bd3/Qc2, target Black's slight queenside pawn deficit.
subVariations.blackPlan: Maneuver knight via Nd7-f8, control e-file with ...Re8, activate bishop on d6.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Gurgenidze System (3.Nc3 g6)
subVariations.description: Bukhuti Gurgenidze's hypermodern concept: Black fianchettoes on g6 and establishes an unbreakable knight outpost on f5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control the center with d4/e5, push g4 to challenge the f5 knight.
subVariations.blackPlan: Anchor knight on f5, trade light bishop for f3 knight, break with ...c5.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Accelerated Panov (2.c4 d5)
subVariations.description: White plays 2.c4 immediately, leading to unique Queen checks on a4 and IQP dynamics.
subVariations.whitePlan: Defend d5 pawn with Bc4, maintain spatial pressure, control central files.
subVariations.blackPlan: Fianchetto on g7, maneuver knight via Nbd7-b6 to win back the d5 pawn.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Hillbilly Attack (2.Bc4 d5 3.Bb3)
subVariations.description: Magnus Carlsen's practical blitz weapon, offering the e4 pawn for fast development and kingside attacking diagonals.
subVariations.whitePlan: Attack Black's king with Qh4, Bh6, and open f-file.
subVariations.blackPlan: Solidify with ...g6 and ...Bg7, coordinate pieces safely, utilize extra material.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Breyer Variation (2.d3 d5 3.Nd2)
subVariations.description: White avoids main line theory and adopts a King's Indian Attack setup against the Caro-Kann.
subVariations.whitePlan: Build kingside attack with Nf1-g3, e5 push, and h4/Nh2.
subVariations.blackPlan: Occupy center with ...e5/d5, develop solidly with ...Bd6 and ...Nbd7.

subVariations.name: Caro-Kann Tartakower 4...Nd7 System
subVariations.description: White targets f7 with Bc4 and Ng5, while Black repels the assault with ...Nb6 and counterstrikes with ...c5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Pressure f7 and e6, maintain dominating knight on e5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Repel White's knights with ...h6, break with ...c5, trade pieces on e5.
